title: Sheaves of modules on a site form a symmetric monoidal closed category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ be the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The tensor product $\otimes_{\mathcal O}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with unit $\mathcal O$ and the associativity, symmetry and unit isomorphisms induced by those of modules over each $\mathcal O(U)$, makes $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ a symmetric monoidal category, additive in each variable. It is closed: for all $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ there is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal G,\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H))$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], natural in all three variables, so $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$ is left adjoint to $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,-)$.

source.place: Lemma 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor), with Section 03EK (tensor product of sheaves of modules on a ringed site)

proof.text: By the tensor-product definition, $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G$ is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor presheaf. The module associativity, symmetry, unit and inverse maps on each section are compatible with restriction, so they are morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules and induce, by the universal property of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], the corresponding sheaf morphisms; the pentagon, hexagon, triangle and involutivity identities can be checked after restricting to sections, where they are the ordinary module identities. Bilinearity gives additivity in each variable.

For sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal H$, the rule $U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O|_U}(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal H|_U)$ with restriction by relocalization is precisely the presheaf $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)$ in the definition. The sheaf-Hom lemma [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-is-sheaf] states that this presheaf is a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules and that its global sections are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)$.

Call a family of $\mathcal O(U)$-bilinear maps $b_U:\mathcal F(U)\times\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal H(U)$ compatible with restriction an $\mathcal O$-bilinear morphism $b:\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$. By the universal property of the tensor product of $\mathcal O(U)$-modules on each section, such $b$ are the same as morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$, and since $\mathcal H$ is a sheaf these are, by the universal property of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], the same as morphisms $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; all identifications are natural. Given $b$, a section $g\in\mathcal G(U)$ gives the $\mathcal O|_U$-linear map $\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal H|_U$ with components $f\mapsto b_V(f,g|_V)$ on $V/U$, an element of $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)(U)$; this is $\mathcal O(U)$-linear in $g$ and compatible with the restriction maps of step 2 [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-is-sheaf], so it is a morphism $\mathcal G\to\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. Conversely, a morphism $c:\mathcal G\to\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H)$ gives the bilinear morphism $b_U(f,g)=c_U(g)_{U/U}(f)$. The two constructions are mutually inverse and natural in $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$, which gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal G,\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal H))$ (this is the item's source, Stacks 03EO, with $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ interchanged by symmetry).

The natural bijection in the preceding step is the adjunction between the functor $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$ and the internal-Hom functor $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,-)$, which is the definition of a closed monoidal category. Thus the additive symmetric monoidal category from step 1 is closed.
